subject: Culture
title: Ancestor Obligations
description: A quick win: understand Ancestor Obligations.

hook.text: In China, you burn paper money so your dead relatives can spend it in the afterlife.

buildup.text: Ancestor veneration spans East Asia, Africa, and Latin America. The dead stay in the family.

discovery.text: Japan's Obon festival welcomes ancestors home each August. Lanterns guide their spirits back.

twist.text: Neglecting ancestors can bring bad luck in many traditions. The dead have expectations.

climax.text: For billions, death isn't departure. It's a change in role—from participant to guardian.

punchline.text: In many families, the dead still have a seat.

quiz.question: During Japan's Obon festival, what do lanterns symbolize?
